name: Fourth Political Theory
summary: The Fourth Political Theory is Aleksandr Dugin's proposal for a politics beyond liberalism, communism and fascism, which takes Heidegger's Dasein, the ethnos or the people rather than the individual, class, race or state as its subject. It rejects liberal individualism, universal human rights, progress and growth, and the unipolar global order, and calls for a return of theology and Tradition, social justice, national sovereignty and a multipolar world of civilisations that judge themselves by their own values. It rejects racism and any ranking of peoples, and invites the Right, the Left and the traditional religions into one front against the liberal West.
scope: Dugin's own theory as the scholarship defines it: Backman (s6, s8) and Auxier (s7) present it as Dugin's, set out in The Fourth Political Theory (2009; Arktos 2012, s5) and developed in his later writings. The profile answers from that book and from Dugin's later texts published on the theory's own site, 4pt.su (the Great Awakening texts, the Greater Europe project, essays on Russia's ideology and three recent interviews). It excludes texts by other 4pt.su authors and adherents, Dugin's earlier neo-Eurasianist geopolitics (Foundations of Geopolitics) and National Bolshevism, which the book calls related but separate theories.

notes: Later pass (rules 5) by claude-opus-5-5. The first pass rested on Wikipedia and three recent interviews; this pass read the full book (archive.org copy of the Arktos edition) and Dugin's own 4PT texts, re-checked every answer and nulled those the sources do not settle (the first pass attributed calls for autarky and economic sovereignty to s3, which contains none). The book gives the theory as parameters rather than a programme, so economics (beyond social justice and the rejection of capitalism and of growth), courts, welfare, taxes, crime and many social-policy questions stay null. Themes searched in the book and the library: economy (market, property, capitalism, socialism, welfare, tax), government (democracy, parties, parliament, monarchy, caste, empire), society (family, gender, religion, race, ethnos, migration), world (multipolarity, war, alliances, UN, nuclear), ecology and technology. Dugin's 2025-26 interviews speak of Russian politics; they are used only where he states a general position. Not reached: the Springer article 'Old wine in a postmodern bottle' (bot check), Millerman's PhilArchive article (bot check) and Shishov's CEU thesis (moved repository); The Rise of the Fourth Political Theory (2017) is not available open-access.
